auths.name: none
auths.explain: No credential; the server is open or trusts the connection.

auths.name: bearer
auths.explain: Sends `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`; the secret is the token.

auths.name: basic
auths.explain: Sends HTTP basic auth; the secret is `user:password`.

auths.name: header
auths.explain: Sends the secret in a header of your choice (auth header name, e.g. X-Api-Key).

auths.name: query
auths.explain: Appends the secret as a query parameter of your choice (auth header name is the parameter).

auths.name: env
auths.explain: Passes the secret to the stdio command as an environment variable (auth header name is the variable).

auths.name: oauth
auths.explain: Signs in with OAuth 2.1 the way the MCP specification describes: PULSE finds the server's authorization server, registers itself as a client when the server allows it (for GitHub, which allows none, it signs in through a public client it carries: a code typed on github.com, nothing to register), opens the sign-in page once (pulse mcp login NAME, or Sign in on the card) and keeps the tokens on this machine, refreshing them itself.
